messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Problem : detectionHistory and detectionMaps
parts:
The problem is the time zone. The record falls between 2 and 3 am on the day the clocks were set forward to summer time. So the record time did not exist in the time zone you selected (CET). And camera traps don't correct for daylight saving time, so record times will be off by one hour.

You could try something like timeZone = "Etc/GMT+1" instead, which doesn't have daylight saving time (or whichever your time zone is relative to UTC).
 
Then will also be issues if the internal clock of some cameras used in your survey were set to winter time, to summer time in others. In such cases the timeShiftImages function (shift date/time of all images from certain cameras) may help to unify these, but there will still be a 1-hour offset during summer time.

If only part of your images needs adjustment (deployment of a camera is partly during winter time, partly summer time, as seems to be the case here), you could try the Adjust Date/Time tool in digiKam. It will update the metadata date/time tag of selected images. When you rerun recordTable the time will be updated. 

Third option, in your record table, you could try adding an hour to all records that fall in summer time, based on the record date/time.

Fourth, if it is urgent, remove that particular record and proceed, knowing that all records during summer time will be off by 1 hour relative to clock time.


Generally handling time zones is a bit of a nuisance, so please give it a good thought before manipulating the data. And if you don't mind, please feel free to share your experiences.

All the best,
Jürgen

Dear Group

As usual Jürgen gives great advice.  

I have a project spanning multiple years where we have locally summer and winter time.  I have long since moved all the camera clock and image work to a fixed single offset from UTC. I leave the cameras set to this time throughout the year(s) and all camptapR and R scripts use this time zone.  I am very careful to specify the time zone  with this format timeZone = "Etc/GMT+1”  every time I deal with POSIXxx dates and time in every R script.  NB. A warning: the sign (+ or -) in the GMT value is the opposite way round to how I think of things - so read the documentation.

In the field I record my date time for the deployments in local time. My GPS data is recorded (by my GPSRx) in two fields as UTC and local time.   I try to make sure these field data do not pollute the electronically-recorded dateTime in the image and camtrapR processing in the creation of the recordTable, above.   I need to be very careful of the dateTime in my excel-created initial station file and as I import it into camtrapR.  I largely achieve this by using the date not the time from the station file once in camtrapR; not the optimal solution. I should maintain both in my station file.
